import { LinkCard } from "@astrojs/starlight/components";

A startup lives by a few numbers: the cost of each request it serves, the accuracy of the feature it sells, the speed of the engine at its core. There are more ideas to try on each of them than people to try them. Thermite puts AI agents on those numbers around the clock, on GPUs you rent by the hour or machines you already have. A judge that the agents can't touch measures every change, so what you ship is what was measured, and you can show the record to a customer or an investor.

## Use cases

Each of these runs on hardware you rent or own, with a budget you set.

- **Software:** [Make your code faster without breaking it](../software/faster-code.md)
- **Software:** [Migrate a codebase until every test passes](../software/migrations.md)
- **AI and machine learning:** [Run a model faster on the GPU you have](../ai/inference-speed.md)
- **AI and machine learning:** [Make your LLM feature score higher on your own tests](../ai/llm-quality.md)
- **Science:** [Make a simulation faster or more accurate](../science/simulations.md)
- **Healthcare and life sciences:** [Improve a segmentation model on scans it never saw](../healthcare/imaging.md)
- **Agriculture:** [Tune a greenhouse climate controller in simulation](../agriculture/greenhouses.md)
- **Energy and buildings:** [Write building and battery controllers, scored in a simulator](../energy/buildings.md)
- **Operations and logistics:** [Pack work onto machines with less waste](../operations/scheduling.md)
- **Operations and logistics:** [Plan delivery routes closer to the best known](../operations/routing.md)
- **Robotics:** [Teach a robot the task, not a loophole](../robotics/rewards.md)
- **Finance:** [Test strategies on years they never saw](../finance/strategies.md)

## Why it fits

- **Rent the GPU, not a platform.** Control launches a rig on RunPod for you, with a spend limit, and stops or terminates it when you say; its results reach control before it goes ([Add a rig on RunPod](../../how-to/install/runpod-rig.md)). A machine of your own joins over SSH ([Add a rig on a machine](../../how-to/install/rig-on-a-machine.md)).
- **You set the spend.** Nothing stops a campaign by default. Set a stop time, a limit on judging hours on the device, or a limit on money spent on the model, and a spent budget pauses the run until you decide ([Set a budget or a stop time](../../how-to/campaigns/budget-and-stop-time.md)).
- **Every win is confirmed before it counts.** The judge measures each change beside the best version so far, confirms a gain on fresh runs and on cases the agents never saw, and keeps its reasons. A change that is faster but wrong never becomes the best version ([Why agents never judge](../../explanation/why-agents-never-judge.md)).
- **Many campaigns at once.** One control runs campaigns on many rigs, and one campaign can run on several rigs to check a result on another machine ([Run a campaign on several rigs](../../how-to/campaigns/several-rigs.md)).
- **The result is yours, in your repository.** Take the best version as a patch, or as a commit on the run's branch in your own repository ([Take the result](../../how-to/campaigns/take-the-result.md)). Your code goes to your rigs and your model endpoint, and nowhere else.
- **Wire it into your tools.** A REST API, MCP and the `thermite` command line start, watch and steer campaigns, so your own scripts and AI assistants can too ([Script Thermite with the REST API](../../how-to/automate/rest-api.md)).

## Get started

1. [Install on one machine](../../tutorials/first-run.md): about twenty minutes, and the judge's smoke check shows a dozen known changes, cheats among them, getting their expected verdicts.
2. [Add a rig on RunPod](../../how-to/install/runpod-rig.md) with a spend limit, or on a machine you own.
3. [Write a kit](../../how-to/campaigns/write-a-kit.md) for the number that matters, and [test it](../../how-to/campaigns/test-a-kit.md) with known changes before any agent sees it.
4. [Write a contract](../../how-to/campaigns/write-a-contract.md) with the guards your customers care about, and [set a budget](../../how-to/campaigns/budget-and-stop-time.md).
5. Start the campaign, and [take the result](../../how-to/campaigns/take-the-result.md) when you are happy with it.

## What to know first

- **One owner for each installation.** A team shares one control, which one owner signs in to; scripts and assistants get tokens of their own ([Tokens and roles](../../reference/tokens.md)).
- **API keys for a team.** A Claude or ChatGPT plan may serve only its owner's own Thermite; a Thermite that several people use takes API keys ([Choose a model](../../how-to/models/choose-a-model.md)).
- **Agents run code that a model wrote.** On RunPod, Thermite adds no network rules, so that code can reach the internet. Read [the security model](../../explanation/security-model.md) and [Known limits](../../reference/known-limits.md).
- **Thermite is 0.x.** Versions make no upgrade promise yet. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0.
